competitors.counterevidence: Pricing reference only. Does not offer automation-specific white-label reports.
competitors.limitation: Price anchor, not WTP proof for this product
competitors.skeptic_review: Intry's $149 tier proves coaching platforms can charge $149/mo. It does not prove coaches will pay for automation-specific reports. Price anchor only.
competitors.missing_perspective: No data on Intry's actual subscriber count, churn, or feature adoption at the $149 tier.
competitors.contrarian_review: If Intry already serves coaches at $149/mo with broad coaching tools, an automation-only report tool may be too narrow to compete.

competitors.skeptic_review: CoachStackHub is a general coaching platform. Its pricing validates the coaching tools market broadly but says nothing about demand for automation-specific reports.
competitors.missing_perspective: No data on CoachStackHub's market share, user count, or whether any users use it for automation-related coaching.
competitors.contrarian_review: General coaching platforms may add automation features as a checkbox, making a standalone automation report tool redundant.

competitors.counterevidence: White-label as a category is not unique. Does not offer automation-specific reports.
competitors.limitation: Adjacent tool, not direct competitor for automation reports
competitors.skeptic_review: Coaching.com proves white-label coaching platforms exist and can charge premium prices. It does not prove that automation-specific white-label reports are a distinct purchasable category.
competitors.missing_perspective: No data on whether Coaching.com users have requested automation exposure features or would pay extra for them.
competitors.contrarian_review: If Coaching.com adds automation reports as a feature, a standalone product loses its differentiation. Platform risk is high.

competitors.offer_summary: Free B2C AI job risk calculator (2017, OG)
competitors.counterevidence: B2C free, not B2B white-label. 8+ years domain authority. Outdated data model.
competitors.limitation: Different segment (B2C), not a competitor for coach white-label reports
competitors.skeptic_review: WillRobotsTakeMyJob has 8+ years of SEO authority and free access. It proves B2C demand for job risk information but says nothing about B2B coach willingness to pay for white-labeled reports.
competitors.missing_perspective: No data on WillRobotsTakeMyJob's traffic, revenue model, or whether coaches use it in their workflow.
competitors.contrarian_review: If coaches already use WillRobotsTakeMyJob for free with clients, they may not pay for a white-labeled version unless it provides significantly more value (source labeling, human-review boundary, proof-pack format).

competitors.offer_summary: Task-level CV analysis, skill overlap, adjacent roles. Free beta.
competitors.counterevidence: Closest direct feature competitor but B2C free beta, not B2B white-label.
competitors.skeptic_review: Kairo is the closest feature competitor (task-level analysis, skill overlap, adjacent roles). But it is B2C free beta — a different segment and business model. Feature overlap does not equal competitive threat in B2B coach market.
competitors.missing_perspective: No data on Kairo's user count, funding, or plans to enter B2B. Could pivot to B2B at any time.
competitors.contrarian_review: If Kairo adds white-label/B2B features, it becomes a direct competitor with a free-tier head start. Bridge role pathfinding is not a defensible moat if Kairo already has it.

competitors.counterevidence: Data source, not a competitor. Product depends on this data.
competitors.skeptic_review: O*NET is a public data source. Using it is not a moat — any competitor can use the same data. The differentiation must be in the analysis layer, not the data source.
competitors.missing_perspective: No data on whether O*NET will continue to be freely available or whether API terms could change.
competitors.contrarian_review: If O*NET adds its own automation exposure scoring or partners with a platform to do so, the product's value proposition collapses to the LLM analysis layer only.
